biography.plain_text: Keith McCaw was an American telecommunications businessman from Seattle and the youngest of four brothers whose family cable interests grew into a cellular fortune. A Colorado College business graduate, he helped expand McCaw's paging operations through acquisitions. His wealth began with a cable-business stake transferred by his father during his lifetime.

long_biography.plain_text:
Skiing drew Keith McCaw into ownership of mountain resorts, including Stevens Pass, Mission Ridge and Schweitzer. After relinquishing his executive responsibilities at McCaw Cellular, he pursued investments through his Seattle holding company, MIG. His property ventures included office buildings at Union Station and Willows Commerce Park, extending his interests beyond communications.

His giving supported young people and Seattle's cultural institutions. With his wife Mary Kay, he contributed to the campaign to rebuild the city's opera house. Matching gifts from his brothers' families formed the campaign's largest private contribution. The resulting performance hall bears their mother's name, Marion Oliver McCaw, and houses Seattle Opera and Pacific Northwest Ballet.

confidence.reason: Dated ownership reporting, family obituary and independent local history support the separate investment and civic-giving narrative.

uncertainties: All current classifications refer to the end of his life in December2002. Later estate transactions are used only to corroborate pre-existing structures. His estate, widow and daughters are distinct asset holders.

Real Estate is the strongest alternative terminal sector, but reported acquisition prices combine financing and partner interests. The evidence does not establish that those assets displaced telecom as the main personal portfolio. Use explicit origin-sector fallback.

Family office principal describes the documented personal holding structure and sustained allocation role, not an assumed modern staffed family office. Investor would be a defensible broader description; the structure-specific label is better supported.

Only the middle initial is securely sourced. Secondary nationality and optional secondary residence remain unverified. The input dates agree with the obituary and contemporary death reporting; no unnecessary correction is proposed.

Forbes exact-profile search preceded enrichment. LinkedIn, Instagram and personal-site searches, then Facebook, X/Twitter, Youtube, TikTok, Wikipedia, Vimeo and Flickr checks produced no authenticated individual link. Third-party memorials and family-foundation references are not personal accounts. Trip Advisor and Zillow yielded no person-relevant lead; no historical MIG company domain was authenticated.
